title: Full vs Incremental Loads in ETL

scenes.say: When moving data, should you overwrite everything, or just update what's changed? Let's break down full versus incremental loads.
A full load wipes and reloads all data every time. Incremental loads only add new or changed records, making them much faster for large datasets.

scenes.title: Full vs Incremental
lines: $ INSERT INTO target SELECT * FROM source;
scenes.say: Here's what that looks like in SQL. Full loads delete and reload everything. Incremental loads use a filter, like updated_at, to only grab new data.

scenes.label: Watermark
scenes.sub: A marker that tracks the latest data processed.
scenes.say: Incremental loads rely on a watermark—a marker, like a timestamp, to track what's already processed.

scenes.question: Can you skip change tracking?
scenes.right: No, reliable change tracking is essential for incremental loads to work correctly.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Can you skip tracking changes with incremental loads? No way. Without it, you risk missing or duplicating data.
